comp_disc_analysis.notes:
[chunk 1/3] This is a DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis section. Pure executive pay mechanics (salary tables, RSU vesting schedules, governance checklists) are boilerplate and excluded. Three SIFI-material signals extracted: (1) AI Revenue customer concentration — AI semiconductor = 55% of semiconductor revenue with rapid growth and unnamed hyperscaler customers implied by "custom AI accelerators or XPUs"; (2) Capex/ROI gap signal embedded in the 2025 Tan PSU Award — the maximum performance target of $120B AI Revenue is ~2x total FY2025 company revenue of $63.9B, with no contracted revenue backing this trajectory disclosed in this section; (3) Execution risk on custom AI accelerator ramp — PSU threshold requires 3x+ FY2025 AI Revenue with new business models (racks/systems/XPUs) not yet at scale. VMware integration revenue dependency also flagged. Compensation peer group listed (Alphabet, Apple, IBM, Oracle, Meta, NVIDIA, etc.) is standard benchmarking boilerplate — not extracted as counterparty relationships. No SPVs, circular investments, or off-balance-sheet entities disclosed in this section.
[chunk 2/3] This is a DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis section. Almost all content is routine executive compensation boilerplate (PSU vesting schedules, TSR performance periods, RSU modifications, severance tables). SIFI-material extractions are limited to: (1) The 2025 Tan PSU Award AI Revenue targets ($60B threshold / $120B maximum) covering FY2028-FY2030 — these are the first public quantification of Broadcom management's internal AI revenue ambitions and represent a meaningful CAPEX_ROI_GAP / EXECUTION_RISK signal since no contracted revenue backstop is disclosed and the performance period hasn't started. (2) Key-person forfeiture risk: the entire $607M max award and the AI revenue execution thesis are forfeited if Tan departs before FY2028 starts. No named AI lab counterparties, no SPVs, no off-balance-sheet entities, no investment disclosures appear in this section.
[chunk 3/3] Source text is a DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis section for Broadcom (AVGO), covering: executive compensation tables (CEO pay ratio 543:1, NEO termination payouts, RSU/PSU acceleration values), equity compensation plan information (VMware Plan assumed via acquisition, Inducement Plan), and security ownership table (Vanguard 9.9%, BlackRock 7.3%, Henry Samueli 1.8% with pledged shares). No SIFI-material entities are present: no named AI lab relationships, no customer/supplier concentration data, no off-balance-sheet SPVs, no circular investment relationships, no capex commitments, no revenue roundtripping, and no hidden leverage arrangements. The VMware acquisition is historical and the equity plan assumption is routine post-M&A boilerplate. The Samueli share pledge (16,175,000 shares as collateral) is notable but sub-threshold for SIFI materiality at ~0.3% of shares outstanding. The 5%+ holders (Vanguard, BlackRock) are passive index investors with no strategic relationship to Broadcom's AI/compute business. Nothing in this section meets the SIFI-material threshold defined in the extraction rules.

related_party.notes: [chunk 1/1] This DEF 14A filing for Broadcom (AVGO) contains no SIFI-material disclosures in the related-party transactions section. The filing discloses only: (1) a boilerplate Audit Committee review procedure for related-party transactions, and (2) a generic arms-length statement about directors/management having relationships with counterparties in the ordinary course of business — with no named counterparties, dollar amounts, SPVs, equity investments, capex commitments, or off-balance-sheet structures disclosed. The Non-GAAP appendix shows FY2025 capex (PP&E purchases) of only $623M — well below hyperscaler thresholds and no counterparty named. No hidden-risk signals of the 8 SIFI types are extractable from this document. The filing is a routine proxy statement (DEF 14A) focused on director elections, say-on-pay, and auditor ratification. Analysts should refer to Broadcom's 10-K (Form 10-K for FY2025) for investment portfolio, debt structure, and material related-party disclosures.
